passages.title: Shared witness and honest confession make fellowship more than a claim
passages.summary: The writer announces what he has heard, seen, and touched: the Word of life. He writes so readers may share fellowship with the Father and the Son. God is light, and in him is no darkness. Anyone who claims fellowship and walks in darkness lies. If we walk in the light, Jesus’ blood cleanses us from all sin. If we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves. If we confess our sins, he is faithful to forgive.
passages.uncertainty: No exact location is assigned to unnamed or heavenly settings.

lds.text: The selected Church lesson connects God's light and love with the conduct described here. Why does honest confession belong within walking in light?

contextNote.title: Shared witness and honest confession make fellowship more than a claim
contextNote.text: Verse 5 gives the message: God is light. Verses 6–10 are five sentences that each begin with “if.” Verse 6 rejects a claim of fellowship made by one who walks in darkness. Verse 7 gives the true case, with two results. Those who walk in the light have fellowship with one another. The blood of Jesus also cleanses them from all sin. So walking in the light does not mean having no sin (verses 8–9).

passages.title: Remaining in the received message requires love amid denial and departure
passages.summary: The writer says he writes so that they will not sin. If anyone sins, Jesus Christ the righteous is an advocate with the Father. Those who know him keep his commandments. The command to love is both old and new. Whoever hates his brother is in darkness. He writes to children, fathers, and young men. They must not love the world, which is passing away. Antichrists have gone out, and the readers should remain in what they heard.
passages.uncertainty: No exact location is assigned to unnamed or heavenly settings.

lds.text: The selected Church lesson connects God's light and love with the conduct described here. How does love for a visible brother test a claim about knowing Christ?

contextNote.title: Remaining in the received message requires love amid denial and departure
contextNote.text: Verse 9 tests a claim to be in the light while hating a brother. The verse says he is still in darkness. Verse 10 gives the opposite case. One who loves his brother remains in the light. Nothing in him causes stumbling. Verse 11 says the hater walks in darkness and cannot see his way. So light and darkness are told apart by conduct toward a brother.

passages.title: Love takes visible form through shared goods rather than claims of belonging alone
passages.summary: The writer marvels that believers are called children of God. When Christ appears, they will be like him. Whoever remains in him does not keep on sinning. The message from the beginning is to love one another. Cain killed his brother, and whoever hates is a murderer. Christ laid down his life, and they should lay down theirs for the brothers. One who has goods and shuts out a needy brother lacks God’s love. God’s command is to believe in his Son and love one another.
passages.uncertainty: No exact location is assigned to unnamed or heavenly settings.

lds.text: The selected Church lesson connects God's light and love with the conduct described here. How can shared goods give visible form to love?

contextNote.title: Love takes visible form through shared goods rather than claims of belonging alone
contextNote.text: Verse 16 defines love by an act: Christ laid down his life for us. Verse 17 brings it down to an ordinary case. Someone has the world’s goods and sees a brother in need. If he closes his heart, how does God’s love remain in him? Verse 18 draws the rule. Love is not in word or tongue only; it is in deed and truth. Verse 19 says this is how they know they are of the truth.

passages.title: Confession and visible love test claims about the unseen God
passages.summary: The writer tells them to test the spirits. Every spirit that confesses Jesus Christ come in the flesh is of God. They should love one another, for love is of God. God showed his love by sending his only Son so that they might live. No one has seen God at any time. If they love one another, God remains in them. God is love, and perfect love casts out fear. We love because he first loved us.
passages.uncertainty: No exact location is assigned to unnamed or heavenly settings.

lds.text: The selected Church lesson connects God's light and love with the conduct described here. Why does hatred toward a brother contradict professed love for God?

contextNote.title: Confession and visible love test claims about the unseen God
contextNote.text: Verse 12 says no one has seen God at any time. That makes a claim to love God hard to check. Verse 20 supplies the check. A brother can be seen. One who does not love a seen brother cannot love the unseen God. A man who says he loves God and hates his brother lies. Verse 21 makes it a command: love God, and love a brother also.

passages.title: Shared testimony supports confidence while prayer remains directed by God's will
passages.summary: The writer says whoever believes that Jesus is the Christ is born of God. Loving God means keeping his commandments, and they are not heavy. Faith is the victory that overcomes the world. Jesus Christ came by water and blood, and the Spirit testifies. God has given eternal life, and this life is in his Son. The writer wants believers to know that they have eternal life. They may ask according to God’s will and be heard. He ends by telling the little children to keep themselves from idols.
passages.uncertainty: No exact location is assigned to unnamed or heavenly settings.

lds.text: The selected Church lesson connects God's light and love with the conduct described here. How does asking according to God's will shape confidence in prayer?

contextNote.title: Shared testimony supports confidence while prayer remains directed by God's will
contextNote.text: Verse 13 gives the writer’s purpose: that believers know they have eternal life. Verse 14 names what follows from that knowledge: boldness toward God. The boldness is about prayer. The verse sets one condition: asking “according to his will.” Under that condition, he listens. Verse 15 adds that if he listens, they have what they asked. Verse 16 gives a first use: asking life for a brother who sins.

words.label: Anoint
words.meaning: To pour oil on a person or thing to set it apart. Kings and priests were anointed.

words.label: Antichrist
words.meaning: One who opposes Christ. First John 2:22 uses the word for those who deny him.
